findings.title: Per-class fixture-builder helper is copy-pasted verbatim into multiple sibling test modules in this chunk
findings.evidence: `fn human_barbarian_input(level: u8) -> CharacterInput` is defined identically 3 times in this chunk (line 60432 in `barbarian_dispatch_widening_safety_tests`, line 61594 in `raging_climber_and_swimmer_tests`, line 61789 in `barbarian_rage_power_superstition_tests`) -- each body is the same 6-line `load_character_input_fixture(...) -> assert diagnostics empty -> set class_levels -> return input`. `fn human_skald_input` is duplicated at lines 60688 and 61603. `fn human_alchemist_input` is duplicated at lines 63531 and 63991. `fn human_inquisitor_input` is duplicated at lines 64326 and 65330. That is 4 of 20 fixture-builder-owning modules in this chunk (4 of 20) whose builder body already exists elsewhere in the same file.
findings.risk_notes: Each copy lives in a separate #[cfg(test)] mod with its own `use super::{...}` import list, so collapsing them is a real refactor (shared test-support module + re-export), not a mechanical cargo-check-provable deletion.

findings.title: Repo-wide test-boilerplate pattern (per-class fixture const + builder fn) is a natural extraction seam
findings.evidence: The 3-line `const FIGHTER_LEVEL_1_FIXTURE: &str = include_str!("../../../tests/fixtures/.../pf1_human_fighter_level1_ge06_deterministic_input.txt")` block appears 74 times in the whole 78,506-line file, 20 of those 74 inside this chunk (lines 60006-69571), one per `#[cfg(test)] mod <class>_..._tests`. Each module also redeclares its own `human_<class>_input(level) -> CharacterInput` builder (20 in this chunk, listed in lane_summary.cross_chunk). None of these differ except the class-id constant they set.
findings.risk_notes: Consolidating into one shared `pilot_compute::test_support` module (one fixture const, one `human_class_input(class_id, level)` builder used by every class module) would cut roughly 10-15 boilerplate lines per module across dozens of modules file-wide without touching any assertion logic. Out of auto-fix scope per ground rules (not a pure deletion), but low-risk to do by hand since each site is mechanically identical.

findings.title: Roughly a quarter of this 78.5k-line 'production surface' file is inline #[cfg(test)] modules
findings.evidence: This chunk alone (60006-69571, 9,566 of 78,506 total lines = 12% of the file) contains 20 `#[cfg(test)] mod` blocks and zero non-test top-level items (no `fn`/`struct`/`enum`/`impl` starting at column 0 in the whole 60000-70000 line band). The `_dispatch_widening_safety_tests` naming convention alone recurs 38 times file-wide (grep count), suggesting the test-module fraction of the file is large well beyond this chunk.
findings.risk_notes: Moving these to `tests/` integration files (one per class, or grouped by era) would shrink mod.rs substantially and make the production-vs-test boundary of this 78.5k-line accretion file legible again; needs a companion audit of what `super::{...}` imports actually require (some reach private items only visible via inline placement).

findings.title: Nine near-identical 'actively judging <type>' Inquisitor tests could partly collapse into a data-driven case list
findings.evidence: single_class_inquisitor_actively_judging_{justice,protection,purity,smiting,destruction,healing,piercing,resiliency,resistance}_with_recognized_choice_applies_real_bonus (9 functions spanning lines 64390-64931) share identical setup (push a judgment SelectedChoice + push an EquippedActive ability activation, call build_pilot_headless_receipt, assert Blocked on other_features_deferred) and differ only in which selection id is pushed and which explanation/total field is asserted afterward.
findings.risk_notes: Not a clean 1:1 table collapse like the oracle module's own `each_new_mystery_reaches_computed_with_a_curse` loop (line 68469) achieved, because each arm also asserts a different negative-leak check on a different sibling total (attack bonus vs AC vs saves) -- a naive loop would need a richer per-case struct (selection id, positive-check id+value, negative-check id+value) to avoid losing that per-judgment-specific leak guard.

Duplicate-candidate const: `const FIGHTER_LEVEL_1_FIXTURE: &str = include_str!("../../../tests/fixtures/rules_core/pf1_human_fighter_level1_ge06_deterministic_input.txt")` -- 74 occurrences file-wide, 20 in this chunk, one per test module. Same extraction seam as the builder-fn finding above.
